title: Cohomology over an open etale object is cohomology on the open scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For every $q\geq0$, cohomology over the object $j:U\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is canonically isomorphic to $H^q(U_{\mathrm{Et}},j^{-1}G)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], via the equivalence of the localized site $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$ with the small etale site $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The isomorphisms are natural in $G$ and in restriction along inclusions of open subschemes. If $G=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and $\kappa_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*\mathcal F$ is the natural open-immersion pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], then $j^{-1}G$ identifies naturally with $(\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module].

proof.text: Use the existing exact extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction on abelian etale sheaves, Etale.openImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction and preservesFiniteLimits_openImmersionLowerShriek. Restriction also has a right adjoint, localizationRestrictionLowerStarAdjunction, hence is exact. This is precisely the mechanism of Stacks 03F3, without constructing the intermediate slice-site comparison.

Let A_j be the sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on uliftYoneda(j). The sheafification/free-abelian/ulift-Yoneda adjunction identifies Hom(A_j,G) additively with G(j). The extension-by-zero adjunction and the constant-sheaf adjunction at id_U identify Hom(j_! Z_U,G) with the same sections. The iso mk(id_U composed with j) to mk(j) handles the identity composition. The public EtaleOpenComparison.sectionsEquiv, restrictedSectionsEquiv, and representingHomEquiv prove these identifications and their naturality in G. Coyoneda.ext yields the actual isomorphism A_j to j_! Z_U; no arbitrary witness is chosen.

Apply the exact Ext adjunction to Z_U and G. Precomposition with representingIso gives Ext^q(A_j,G) isomorphic to Ext^q(j_!Z_U,G), then the inverse Ext adjunction identifies this with Ext^q(Z_U,j^*G), which is Sheaf.H of the restricted sheaf. The same constructed equivalence is exposed as etaleCohomologyOverOpenEquiv, and etaleCohomologyOverOpenEquiv_naturality proves coefficient naturality via the source mapExtCounit_comp_mk₀ and Ext associativity. The publicly imported named obligation etaleCohomologyOverOpenEquiv_restriction records commutativity with the free-sheaf object map and the independently constructed canonical global restriction map. Step 4 covers the remaining quasi-coherent clause using the publicly imported etaleTensorSectionsSheaf_openIdentification; no prose clause is omitted.

Set $G=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$. For each etale $v:V\to U$, the restriction functor of step 1, evaluated sectionwise as in step 2, gives $(j^{-1}G)(V)=G(j\circ v)=\Gamma(V,(j\circ v)^*\mathcal F)$. Apply $c_{v,j}^{-1}$ to identify this with $\Gamma(V,v^*j^*\mathcal F)$ and then $v^*(\kappa_{\mathcal F}^{-1})$ to identify it with $\Gamma(V,v^*(\mathcal F|_U))=((\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}})(V)$. Naturality of $c_{v,j}$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal F}$ makes these maps commute with each restriction $\rho_g$, whose formula and composition law are given by the etale quasi-coherent presheaf nodes. Thus the sectionwise maps form the stated natural isomorphism of sheaves. The Lean clause is the publicly imported named obligation etaleTensorSectionsSheaf_openIdentification. Its conclusion includes the component formula with the inverse normalized tensorSectionsComp and tensor pullback of the inverse canonical restriction/pullback comparison, so the identification is specified rather than an arbitrary sheaf isomorphism.
